newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen having upward bias.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen having upward bias.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to test the upside on Thursday as the market looks to stocks for clues to direction, traders said.
The June will probably open higher, as Tokyo share prices are likely to decline after a steep fall in U.S. share prices overnight, they said.

"Tokyo share prices are likely to open below 20,000... The June will probably be bought at the outset, but meet resistance near the previous day's high (of 124.71)," said a senior trader at a city bank's securities unit.
The market will also focus on the results of a six-year JGB auction due at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT).
Traders said the coupon rate for the new six-year bonds is likely to be set at around 1.8 percent. The issue amount is expected to be 500 billion yen, they said.
One key for the JGB market will be whether demand for cash bonds re-emerges, traders said.
"Few people tried to buy back cash bonds when the market was falling sharply, but demand may increase once JGBs begin rising again," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
The first trader said that there seemed to have been more selling than buying of cash JGBs recently.
"There was strong selling pressure on cash bonds such as the 193rd and 194th 10-year JGBs on Wednesday," the trader said.
